body:
## Why

A decomposed track is only legible as text today: `hkb list` shows `⇐ #101,#100` and the drawer shows a
"Blocked by" list. Reconstructing a diamond from that is work a picture would do for free, and the
maintainer is a visual thinker. Value 4: a rung that is possible but tedious is a gap to close.

The decisive fact: **the graph is already on the wire.** `src/serve.js:96` already puts
`blockedBy: [{number, title, done}]` on every card in the `/api/board` payload. The page already renders
those as chips and as a "Blocked by" list, and blocker titles are already clickable through a
`data-open="<n>"` handler that reopens the drawer on that card. Drawing the subgraph needs **no new
route, no new fetch, no new server call, no new dependency and no new file** — it is a rendering change
over data that is already fetched, already tested and already polled.

Put it in the drawer, not behind the board: the drawer is where you already land when you ask "what is
this card waiting on", it is scoped to one root so 5-15 nodes is the honest common case, and clicking a
node reuses wiring that exists today.

## What

An inline SVG of the focused card's dependency subgraph, above the existing "Blocked by" section:
the card itself, everything it is transitively blocked by, and the root it blocks if there is one.

- Nodes fill from the existing status custom properties (`var(--ready)`, `var(--running)`, …) so the
  graph matches the columns with **no new palette**. Done blockers are dimmed and keep their `✓`; the
  focused card is outlined.
- Clicking a node opens that card in the drawer — **reuse the existing `data-open="<n>"` handler**
  (`web/index.html`, the blocked-by list). Do not add a second open path.
- Layout is a top-level function in the page's **existing single classic `<script>`**: longest-path
  layering, then one or two barycenter ordering passes.
- Nothing renders when a card has neither blockers nor a blocked parent — no empty box.

**The landmine, verified — do not step on it.** Do *not* introduce `<script type="module">` with a
relative `import`. It passes the four self-containment regexes in `test/serve.test.js`, but a top-level
`import` makes `new vm.Script(PAGE_SCRIPT)` throw and breaks all five `loadPage` tests, which use
`vm.runInContext` — a classic-script evaluator that cannot load a module. Keep the layout inside the
existing classic script as a top-level function; that is how `mdLite`, `esc` and the render path are
reached from the vm harness today. CLAUDE.md's "pure logic goes in `src/model.js`" is real, but
`web/index.html` is an existing tested-in-vm exception — do not create a second copy of the algorithm
in `src/model.js`, and do not add a static asset route to honour the letter of the rule.

**The incomplete-history case.** Where the GraphQL `blockedBy` field is unavailable, `src/tasks.js:94`
REST-fills only `todo`/`blocked` cards, so edges to *already-closed* blockers are missing. Show a
one-line note that the history is incomplete rather than drawing a confidently wrong picture.
**Do not widen `fillBlockedByRest`** — it is a per-task REST call and violates Values 2 and 3.

## Done when

- Opening a card in the drawer shows its subgraph as inline SVG, with the behaviours above.
- `test/serve.test.js` asserts layer assignment, node count and edge count on a fixture containing a
  **diamond**, reached from the vm harness, **without a DOM**.
- Graph data comes only from the `/api/board` payload — no change to `src/serve.js`, none to `src/tasks.js`.
- The four existing self-containment assertions still pass unchanged: exactly one `<script`, no `src=`,
  no `https?:` in `src|href`, no protocol-relative URL.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green.
- `docs/wiki/features/web-board.md` updated and `node .repolore/scripts/wiki-check.mjs` clean.

## Known limitation, accept it

Barycenter ordering measured ~6.8 average crossings on random 12-node DAGs. This is a *readable* graph
at 5-15 nodes, not a pretty one at 30. Do not gold-plate the layout to chase that; if it proves
unreadable on a real decomposition, the follow-up is a separate vendored `web/mermaid.min.js` on its own
ETag'd route — never inline, never a CDN.
goal: opening a card in the hkb serve drawer shows its dependency subgraph as inline SVG, no new dependency
title: See the subgraph: a dependency graph in the board drawer
